gaps.category: Verifier suppression: 'example/test/dummy' context heuristic kills real findings (8 risk files)
gaps.why_missed: The detector actually FOUND the risk secret in all 8 files (visible in the report's 'suppressed' array). The benchmark ran `klarion scan --no-ai`, which routes findings through the offline heuristic verifier (internal/verify/heuristic.go). Rule 3 there marks any 'generic*'-rule finding false_positive (confidence 0.75) when contextMarkers ('test', 'example', 'sample', 'dummy', ...) appear in the FILE PATH or the ±3-line context snippet. Leaky-repo credentials sit next to `example.com` hostnames and `*@example.com`/`dummy@example.com` emails (normal in server/deploy configs), and putty-example.ppk has 'example' in its filename, so every hit — docker `auth` base64 blobs, HEROKU_API_KEY, `"password": "hunter22"`, npm `_auth`, and all 20 PPK key-body entropy hits — was flipped to FP. FilterFalsePositives (internal/verify/apply.go, on by default with min_confidence 0.6) then silently dropped them.
gaps.suggested_fix: Highest-leverage single change (+8 risk files, recall 0.43→0.62). In heuristicVerifier.classify: (1) restrict the non-prod-context FP to entropy-only 'generic-high-entropy' findings, never keyword-anchored assignment rules (generic-password-assignment / generic-secret-assignment matched an explicit `password:`/`auth:` key — a nearby example.com hostname is not evidence the VALUE is fake); (2) only honor markers found in the file path or the secret value itself, not neighboring context lines, and stop treating bare 'example.com' host/email strings as markers; (3) or lower context-only FP confidence to <0.6 so the default filter keeps them, and consider defaulting ai.filter_false_positives=false when the verifier is the offline heuristic (its own doc comment promises 'never a silent false-positive').

gaps.category: Structured credential-file formats with no key[:=]value shape (netrc/pgpass/esmtprc/URL-userinfo/FileZilla XML) (6 risk files)
gaps.why_missed: Both generic rules in internal/rules/builtin.go require a `[:=]` separator after the keyword. .netrc (`machine ... login ... password pass123`) and .esmtprc (`password "password"`) are whitespace-separated; db/.pgpass is positional colon-separated (`host:port:db:user:password`) with no key names at all; .git-credentials is a URL userinfo credential (`https://user:pass@github.com`) and only postgres/mysql/mongodb/redis URI rules exist; FileZilla stores `<Pass>ExamplePas123</Pass>` / `<Pass encoding="base64">Njll...</Pass>` as XML ELEMENTS — 'pass' is not in the (password|passwd|pwd) alternation, and the base64 blob's normalized Rényi score is 0.852, below both entropy-sweep thresholds (0.88 keyword / 0.95 no-context). Secondary kills: `pass123` is 7 chars < the {8,80} minimum, and the literal value `password` is in the rule's own allowlist.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add filename-gated rules (rules.Rule needs a path-glob predicate — config.MatchGlob already exists and can gate rules the way IgnorePaths are matched): `.netrc|_netrc` → `(?i)\bpassword\s+(\S+)`; `.pgpass` → `^[^:#\s]+:[^:]*:[^:]*:[^:]*:(.+)$`; `.esmtprc` → `(?i)^\s*password\s+"?([^"\s]+)`; FileZilla XML → `<Pass(?:\s[^>]*)?>([^<]{4,})</Pass>`. Add a filename-independent url-userinfo rule `\b[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://[^:/@\s]+:([^@\s]+)@` (excluding schemes already covered) for .git-credentials. Also add a PuTTY rule anchored on `^PuTTY-User-Key-File-\d+:` (analogous to the PEM private-key rule) so putty-example.ppk is caught structurally. IMPORTANT: give these specific rule IDs (not 'generic-*') — heuristic verifier rules 2–3 only fire on generic-prefixed IDs, so specific rules bypass the example-context and sha/UUID suppressions; note .netrc/.esmtprc/.ftpconfig/filezilla.xml all contain 'example' markers and would otherwise be re-suppressed until gap #1 is fixed. Caveat: `password`/`ExamplePas123` values will still (correctly) trip value-level placeholder checks; recovering those specific GT lines requires trusting the file format over the value.

gaps.category: Language/function-call credential syntax and punctuation-rich secrets invisible to line regex + tokenizer (4 risk files)
gaps.why_missed: Four independent regex-shape failures, verified against the detector: (1) wp-config.php `define( 'DB_PASSWORD', 'admin' )` and all 8 AUTH_KEY/SALT defines separate key and value with a comma, which `["'\s]*[:=]` cannot match; (2) the WP salts (and Django's SECRET_KEY value `zh!=!gq(w^_t[sBR29954x)...`) are full of spaces and punctuation, so the generic-secret capture class `[A-Za-z0-9_\-+/=.]` stops at the first special char AND the entropy-sweep tokenizer `[A-Za-z0-9+_-]{16,}` (detector.go tokenRe) finds zero tokens ≥16 chars in any of them (verified); (3) Django's `SECRET_KEY = ` matches the alternation's 'secret' but the literal `_KEY` between keyword and `=` breaks `["'\s]*[:=]` — there is no `secret[_-]?key` variant; (4) salesforce.js passes creds as positional args `conn.login('user', 'salesforcepassword', ...)` — no key name, no separator; the value also has no digits (entropy.require_digit=true) and is 18 chars < entropy min_length 20; (5) config.php `$dbpasswd = 'pass123'` DID match via 'passwd' but 'pass123' is 7 chars, below the value's {8,80} floor.
gaps.suggested_fix: (a) Extend the generic-secret alternation with `secret[_-]?key` and allow `[a-z0-9_]{0,20}` filler between keyword and separator (the provider-contextual rules already do this). (b) Accept `,` as a separator and quoted values: keyword `["'\s]*[:=,]\s*(['\"])([^'\"]{6,})\1` — quoted capture is the only way to see punctuation/space-rich secrets like WP salts; entropy-gate it at ~0.6 to control noise. (c) Add a high-precision WordPress rule: `define\(\s*['\"](?:DB_PASSWORD|(?:SECURE_|LOGGED_IN_|NONCE_)?AUTH_(?:KEY|SALT)|LOGGED_IN_(?:KEY|SALT)|NONCE_(?:KEY|SALT))['\"]\s*,\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]` with a non-generic ID. (d) Positional-arg logins (jsforce et al.) are the hardest; either a narrow `\.login\(\s*['\"][^'\"]+['\"]\s*,\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]` rule or leave to the AI verify pass. (e) Lower the {8,80} password floor to {6,80} (pass123-class secrets) — the entropy floor still filters trivial values.

gaps.category: Detector placeholder/entropy gates rejecting real-but-encoded or theme-named secrets (3 risk files)
gaps.why_missed: All three matched a rule's regex, then died in acceptRuleMatch/isPlaceholder (detector.go): (1) ventrilo `Password=UserPassword123` passes the 0.5 entropy floor (score 0.911, verified) but isPlaceholder's SUBSTRING stopword check hits builtin stopword 'password123' (config.go builtinStopwords) — the whole value is discarded; (2) Firefox `"encryptedPassword": "MDoEEPgAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAEw..."` matched generic-password, but NSS/DER base64 legitimately starts with a 19-char run of 'A', tripping maxRepeatRun≥5 → placeholder (verified); (3) JetBrains WebServers.xml `password="dff9dfdfdfda..."` matched, but the XOR-obfuscated hex scores 0.499 — one thousandth below the 0.5 entropy floor — and its 9 distinct chars also fail the distinct<12 placeholder check (verified). These are systematic: browser password stores and IDE configs deliberately store low-entropy-looking encodings.
gaps.suggested_fix: (1) Make the stopword check anchored for rule-based matches: reject only if the value minus a numeric suffix EQUALS a stopword (or matches `^(?:user|admin)?password\d*$`), not substring-contains — 'UserPassword123' as a whole is a plausible real password. (2) Skip repeat-run/distinct-count placeholder heuristics when the matched key name is explicitly password/encryptedPassword (pass the key context into acceptRuleMatch). (3) Add anchored format rules with no entropy floor (fixed formats, per the file's own design note): `"encrypted(?:Username|Password)"\s*:\s*"([A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,})"` for Firefox logins.json, and `<fileTransfer[^>]*\bpassword="([0-9a-f]{16,})"` for .idea/WebServers.xml.

gaps.category: Key-name coverage gap: 'pass', 'passphrase', '*_PASS' not in the password alternation (2 risk files)
gaps.why_missed: .ftpconfig uses `"pass": "hunter22"` and `"passphrase": "swordfish"`; the hub/IRC `config` file uses `IRC_PASS=irc_pass`. The generic-password rule's keyword prescreen AND regex alternation are exactly (password|passwd|pwd) — bare 'pass', 'passphrase' and '_PASS' never enter the rule. The values themselves would have passed: hunter22 scores 0.976 normalized entropy (verified). The entropy sweep can't save them either (hunter22/swordfish/irc_pass are all <16 chars, below tokenizer minimum).
gaps.suggested_fix: Broaden the alternation to `(?i)(?:\b|_)(?:pass(?:word|wd|phrase|code)?|pwd)["'\s]*[:=]` — the existing 0.5 entropy floor, allowlist, and length bounds keep bare-'pass' false positives in check. Note the interplay with gap #1: .ftpconfig has `"host": "example.com"` two lines above the password, so after this fix the finding would STILL be verifier-suppressed under --no-ai until the context heuristic is repaired (or the rule gets a non-generic ID).

gaps.category: Verifier identifier-shape heuristics: UUID and 40-hex treated as 'not a credential' (1 risk file, +1 shared)
gaps.why_missed: Real token formats collide with 'identifier' shapes. hub's `oauth_token: "7f9cc25de..."` was detected (entropy 1.00) but GitHub OAuth tokens are exactly 40 hex chars, so heuristic.go's hex40Re branch FP'd it as 'a git-sha-like 40-char hex digest' (confidence 0.7 ≥ the 0.6 filter bar). Likewise npm legacy `_authToken=<uuid-shaped-token-redacted>` IS UUID-shaped, so uuidRe FP'd it as 'a UUID, not a credential' (.npmrc's other hit was killed by the gap-#1 context heuristic, so the file shows in both).
gaps.suggested_fix: Shape alone must not overrule key context. In heuristicVerifier.classify, before FP-ing UUID/40-hex generic matches, check the request context/line for credential key names (token|auth|password|secret|apikey): `oauth_token:` and `_authToken=` should yield secret/uncertain. Only apply the git-sha demotion when the context mentions commit/sha/rev/ref (the detector's own skipGeneric already does exactly this correctly with gitShaContext — the verifier should mirror it instead of matching bare shape).

klarionMisses.narrative:
Klarion missed 24 of 42 risk-bearing files in leaky-repo (risk_file_recall 0.43). I reproduced the benchmark run exactly (`./klarion scan --no-ai -f json`, 98 findings in 20 files, matching benchmark/results/accuracy.json) and then scanned every missed file individually, inspecting both the reported findings and the JSON `suppressed` array. This split the 24 misses cleanly into two failure planes.

PLANE 1 — THE VERIFIER, NOT THE DETECTOR (9 files: both .docker files, heroku.json, deployment-config.json, sftp-config.json, .vscode/sftp.json, .npmrc, putty-example.ppk, hub). The detector correctly found the risk secret in all nine; the offline heuristic verifier (internal/verify/heuristic.go — used because the benchmark passed --no-ai) marked them false_positive and apply.go's FilterFalsePositives (default on, min_confidence 0.6) silently dropped them. Two heuristics are responsible: (a) the 'test/example/docs context' rule, which matches markers like 'example' and 'dummy' against the file path AND the ±3-line context snippet — leaky-repo's `example.com` hostnames and `dummy@example.com` emails sit right next to real passwords, and putty-example.ppk has 'example' in its name (8 files); (b) shape heuristics that FP any UUID or 40-hex generic match — but npm legacy _authTokens ARE UUIDs and GitHub oauth_tokens ARE 40-hex (hub, plus .npmrc's second hit). Fixing the context heuristic alone recovers 8 files (recall 0.43 → 0.62); with the shape fix, 9 (→ 0.64). This is the cheapest, highest-leverage fix and it is a prerequisite for several detector-side fixes below: .netrc, .esmtprc, .ftpconfig, filezilla.xml, config, and salesforce.js all contain 'example' markers, so new generic-rule matches there would be re-suppressed. (Alternatively: give new rules non-'generic-' IDs, since isGenericRule() gates those verifier heuristics by rule-ID prefix.)

PLANE 2 — THE DETECTOR NEVER FIRED (15 files), for four distinct reasons. (1) Structured formats without key[:=]value shape (6 files): netrc/esmtprc are space-separated, .pgpass is positional, .git-credentials is a URL-userinfo credential, FileZilla uses `<Pass>` XML elements — the generic rules in internal/rules/builtin.go hard-require `[:=]` after (password|passwd|pwd), and no url-basic-auth or PPK rule exists. (2) Language syntax + punctuation secrets (4 files): PHP `define('DB_PASSWORD', 'admin')` and jsforce `conn.login(user, pass)` use commas/positional args; Django's `SECRET_KEY` breaks the regex because '_KEY' sits between the 'secret' keyword and '='; and I verified the WP salts and Django key contain ZERO tokens ≥16 chars under the tokenizer `[A-Za-z0-9+_-]{16,}` — punctuation-rich secrets are invisible to the entropy sweep by construction. (3) Placeholder/entropy gates eating real encoded secrets (3 files): 'UserPassword123' dies on the substring stopword 'password123' despite scoring 0.911; Firefox NSS base64 ('MDoEEP' + 19×'A') dies on the repeat-run≥5 check; JetBrains XOR-hex scores 0.499, one thousandth under the 0.5 floor, and also fails the distinct-char check. (4) Key-name gaps (2 files): 'pass', 'passphrase', 'IRC_PASS' are simply not in the alternation, though their values (hunter22 = 0.976) would pass every other gate.

Priority order by cost: verifier context suppression (8) > structured formats (6) > language syntax/tokenizer (4) > placeholder gates (3) > key-name gap (2) > shape heuristics (1). A realistic bundle — verifier context+shape fixes, filename-gated rules for .netrc/.pgpass/.esmtprc/FileZilla/PPK plus a url-userinfo rule, a WordPress define() rule, quoted-value capture, and the broader pass* alternation — plausibly recovers ~20 of 24 files (recall → ~0.9); the stragglers are values that genuinely look like placeholders ('password', 'ExamplePas123', 'admin'), where the benchmark's ground truth and any sane FP policy are in direct tension. Key source files: internal/verify/heuristic.go (both verifier gaps), internal/verify/apply.go (silent FP filtering), internal/rules/builtin.go (generic rule shapes), internal/detect/detector.go (tokenizer, isPlaceholder, stopword substring check), internal/config/config.go (builtinStopwords incl. 'password123'; entropy thresholds 0.88/0.95, min_length 20, require_digit).

issues.description: ripsecrets never scans hidden files or dot-directories (its default pre-commit walk via the Rust `ignore` crate skips hidden entries, and there is no CLI flag in v0.1.11 to change it). Evidence from raw outputs: zero dotfile findings across all three corpora; it flags '-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----' in leaky/misc-keys/cert-key.pem but reports nothing for the identical pattern in leaky/.ssh/id_rsa, and misses the .npmrc npm token that gitleaks/trufflehog/klarion catch. 21 of 44 ground-truth files (~48%), including most risk files, are dotfiles or live under dot-directories, so they were never even read by ripsecrets.
issues.impact: ripsecrets' published leaky scores (file_coverage_pct 9.09, risk_file_recall 0.0952, F1 0.1739) measure file-traversal policy, not detection ability, yet accuracy.json presents them head-to-head with tools that scan dotfiles. The harness docstring and results carry no disclosure. Cross-tool ranking on leaky is misleading for this one tool.

issues.description: No deduplication of trufflehog decoder duplicates, and a deviation from official benchmark.py trufflehog semantics. In raw/trufflehog-leaky.out the same secrets in .bashrc are reported twice (PLAIN + ESCAPED_UNICODE decoders): Mailchimp at lines 106 and 107, Github at 109 and 110 (actual lines are 106/109, so the ESCAPED_UNICODE duplicates are also off by one line). The harness counts every JSONL record, so total_findings=12 and capped_finds=12 include 2 duplicates (10 unique); deduped find_coverage_pct would be 5.71% not 6.86%. rails also has a duplicate (guides/source/action_mailbox_basics.md:241 URI twice; 9 vs 8 unique). Note the official benchmark.py used assignment semantics per path (finds[path] = len(stringsFound)), not accumulation, though for trufflehog v2's different output format.
issues.impact: Slight inflation of trufflehog's find coverage on leaky and noise count on rails; duplicate rows with inconsistent (off-by-one) line numbers in the published findings lists. File-level metrics (coverage, recall, precision) are unaffected because dedup only changes within-file counts.

issues.description: Effective scan scope differs by tool defaults, so the clean-corpus 'noise' comparison is partially a traversal-scope comparison. klarion (the project's own tool) ships default ignore_paths (internal/config/config.go Default(): *.lock, go.sum, *.svg, *.min.js, *.map, images, binaries, plus a 1 MB size cap) and scanned only 104/236 flask files and 4790/4967 rails files, while detect-secrets --all-files and gitleaks dir scan everything. Verified material effect on these corpora is small: gitleaks/detect-secrets had zero findings in klarion-skipped file types, but ripsecrets' rails noise includes 7 findings in guides/assets/images/*.svg that klarion never scanned, and flask's uv.lock (308 KB of hashes) was excluded from klarion's exposure entirely.
issues.impact: The bias direction favors klarion on the clean-corpus noise metric (fewer files scanned -> less noise possible). Not disclosed in the harness docstring or results. On the current corpora the numeric distortion is limited, but the 'files scanned' asymmetry (104 vs 236, 4790 vs 4967, 46 vs 49) should be reported alongside noise counts.

issues.description: Asymmetric verification treatment: trufflehog's verification is explicitly disabled (--no-verification) 'for parity', but klarion retains its offline heuristic false-positive suppression layer — the harness scores only data['findings'] and silently ignores the raw JSON's top-level 'suppressed' array (39 suppressed on leaky, 17 on flask, 628 on rails, all verdict=false_positive from the 'heuristic' verifier). This is klarion's default output, and on leaky it actually hurts klarion (all 20 candidate findings in GT risk file misc-keys/putty-example.ppk were suppressed as 'test/example/docs context', costing a risk-file detection), but on clean corpora it removes 17 (flask) and 628 (rails) would-be noise findings from klarion's ledger.
issues.impact: klarion's headline clean-corpus noise (1 finding on flask, 93 on rails) is post-filter output competing against other tools' raw detections; e.g. rails would show 721 candidate detections pre-suppression. Defensible as 'default tool behavior' but must be disclosed since the benchmark authors also author klarion; the harness neither reports the suppressed counts nor mentions the layer.

issues.description: Reproducibility hygiene: main() merges via existing.update(results) and accepts a tool subset in argv, so a partial rerun can leave stale sections from older runs mixed into the published accuracy.json; no run timestamps or tool versions are recorded anywhere in the results (klarion reports version 'dev, commit none'). Verified that the CURRENT file is internally consistent — all 15 sections reproduce exactly from raw outputs written in the same one-minute window, and fresh direct reruns of gitleaks 8.30.0 (22 findings, set-identical) and ripsecrets 0.1.11 (byte-identical) reproduce the stored raw outputs — so no stale data is present today.
issues.impact: Future partial reruns could silently publish mixed-version results with no way to detect it from the artifact. Tool versions (gitleaks 8.30.0, trufflehog 3.93.5, detect-secrets 1.5.0, ripsecrets 0.1.11, klarion dev) exist only in my audit, not in the published file.

issues.description: Latent path-normalization aliasing in norm() (run_benchmark.py:50-60): the dataset-name prefix is stripped by plain string match. detect-secrets runs with cwd inside the dataset, so its paths are already dataset-relative; if a scanned repo ever contains a legitimate top-level directory named exactly like the dataset (e.g. a 'flask/' dir at the flask repo root), those paths would be wrongly truncated and merged with other files. Empirically harmless on current corpora: I verified dotfile handling is correct (leaky/.npmrc -> .npmrc; the './'-stripping while-loop cannot mangle names like .git-credentials since they don't start with './'), out_of_gt_files_flagged is empty for every tool, and every normalized flagged path matched a GT path exactly.
issues.impact: No effect on published numbers today; a silent file-attribution bug if datasets/repos with colliding top-level names are added later. Also ripsecrets' line regex ^(.+?):(\d+): would misparse filenames containing ':<digits>:' (none present).

harnessVerification.notes: Recomputation: I re-parsed every raw artifact myself (klarion/gitleaks JSON, trufflehog JSONL, detect-secrets baseline JSON, ripsecrets text) and re-implemented scoring from secrets.csv, then deep-diffed the full recomputed structures (every field including per_file arrays, by_rule, findings lists; excluding wall_seconds) against accuracy.json: 0 diffs across all 5 tools x 3 datasets. Spot values: klarion leaky 98 findings/20 files covered/45.45%/recall 0.4286; gitleaks 22/13/29.55%/0.3095; detect-secrets 46/24/54.55%/0.5476 — all exact. Ground-truth parsing matches official benchmark.py semantics exactly: 44 GT files, 42 risk files, total_expected=175 (risk+informative), capped finds min(found,expected), FP=overage only, files_covered = found!=0, identical rounding. Line handling: harness introduces no off-by-one; spot-checked klarion (.bash_profile:23), gitleaks (.npmrc:9), trufflehog PLAIN (.bashrc:106) against file contents — all 1-based correct; the only line anomaly is trufflehog's ESCAPED_UNICODE decoder artifact (issue 2). Clean-corpus apples-to-apples at tree level confirmed: no .git or .leaky-meta anywhere under scan-targets (find), all tools pointed at identical trees; leaky tree = 44 GT files + 5 benign extras (README.md, LICENSE, .gitattributes, cert9.db, key4.db) that no tool flagged. No detector-disabling flags: --no-ai/--no-verification only disable network verification; detect-secrets 1.5.0 ran its full default plugin set with --all-files (required since .git removed); gitleaks dir mode used default embedded config; exit codes handled correctly. Raw outputs are authentic: fresh direct reruns of gitleaks and ripsecrets on leaky reproduce the stored raw outputs exactly. Deliberate deviation from official methodology worth knowing: the official benchmark.py scans a git repo (gitleaks --repo-path with history; trufflehog v2 git mode), while this harness scans a flattened working tree with dir/filesystem modes — applied equally to all tools and scoring semantics preserved, so I did not count it as an error. recomputed_ok=true because my independent numbers match accuracy.json exactly; the issues listed are fairness/disclosure/latent-robustness findings, not arithmetic ones — the most consequential being ripsecrets' hidden-file skipping (issue 1) and the klarion scope/suppression disclosure gaps (issues 3-4). Key paths: harness benchmark/harness/run_benchmark.py (norm() lines 50-60, score_leaky lines 172-226, update-merge lines 269-272); klarion defaults internal/config/config.go (Default(), ignore_paths, 1MB cap); evidence files under benchmark/results/raw/.

features.tool: Klarion (कवच, Sanskrit "armor") — AI-native secret scanner, module github.com/0x1Adi/Klarion
features.version: dev (2026-07) — version var defaults to "dev" in cmd/klarion/root.go; claude-plugin/plugin.json and CHANGELOG describe an unreleased 0.1.0
features.language: Go 1.25 (go.mod); dependencies limited to spf13/cobra v1.10.2 and BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0 plus stdlib; ships as a single static binary
features.approach: Two-stage pipeline: Stage 1 is fast deterministic detection (83 keyword-gated regex rules with length/allowlist/entropy guards, plus a generic normalized Renyi-entropy sweep — order alpha=2 collision entropy normalized by closed-form ExpectedCollision(n,k), thresholds 0.88 with keyword context / 0.95 without, score clamped to [0,1.25]); Stage 2 sends each candidate with surrounding code context to an AI verifier that returns secret / false_positive / uncertain verdicts with confidence.
features.verification: Does NOT verify secrets are live — live-credential verification (trufflehog-style) is explicitly a roadmap item in DESIGN.md section 13. Instead, "verification" means AI adjudication (internal/verify): a tiny Verifier interface with three implementations — anthropic.go (Anthropic Messages with strict JSON-schema structured outputs, default model claude-haiku-4-5), openai.go (raw-HTTP OpenAI-compatible client that also serves Ollama/vLLM/LiteLLM via base_url; Ollama needs no key), and heuristic.go (offline, no-network fallback scoring structure/placeholder/known-prefix/non-prod-context signals). Candidates are batched (ai.max_batch default 8), verdicts cached by fingerprint+verifier+model (cache.go, never stores the raw secret), on_error="keep" leaves candidates unverified and still failing (fail closed), and uncertain is always treated as a secret. ai.mode auto/on/off controls provider selection. Note: the repo's own benchmark (benchmark/harness/run_benchmark.py) ran `klarion scan --no-ai -f json`, i.e. heuristic-only offline mode, "for parity" with other tools — accuracy.json reflects Stage 1 + heuristic, not LLM adjudication.
features.git_history: Yes, via `klarion git` (cmd/klarion/git.go, internal/git): default scans the staged index (`git diff --cached`, parsing unified diffs into added-line sets so only + lines are scanned); `--history` walks past commits with `git log -p -U0`, limitable by `--max-commits N` and `--since <date/ref>`. Shells out to the git binary rather than a git library. Discrepancy: README/DESIGN document this flag as `git --all`, but the code implements `--history`.
features.precommit: Yes: `klarion protect [dir]` (cmd/klarion/protect.go) writes a pre-commit hook into .git/hooks that runs `klarion git`; refuses to overwrite an existing hook unless `--force`; bypass via deleting the file or `git commit --no-verify`. Separately, `klarion hook --event pre-tool-use [--bash]` is a Claude Code PreToolUse adapter (reads tool-call JSON on stdin, emits permissionDecision allow/deny/ask with a redacted reason; [hook] block_on sets minimum blocking severity; fail_open=true by default so internal errors never block the agent).
features.baseline: Multiple layers (all verified in code): (1) baseline snapshot — `klarion baseline create` writes .klarion-baseline.json as a fingerprint map (internal/baseline Filter suppresses findings whose sha256-based fingerprint is baselined); (2) [allowlist] config — path globs, secret regexes, exact fingerprints, and stopword substrings; (3) inline markers — lines containing `klarion:allow` or `gitleaks:allow` are skipped (internal/detect/detector.go:338); (4) AI verdict filtering — false_positive verdicts with confidence >= min_confidence (default 0.6) are demoted to a suppressed list; (5) entropy pre-filters — UUIDs, git SHAs, content digests, placeholders, require_digit; (6) per-rule allowlist regexes. Fingerprint = sha256(ruleID || path || sha256(secret))[:32], stable across line drift.
features.output_formats: text (default), json, sarif, junit, gitlab — verified in internal/report/report.go New() switch and one file per format (text.go, json.go, sarif.go, junit.go, gitlab.go). Selected via `--format/-f` or [report] format. Secrets redacted by default (raw fields are json:"-"; fixed-width mask); `--show-secrets` overrides. Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 operational error.
features.license: MIT (LICENSE file, Copyright (c) 2026 The Klarion Authors; also declared in plugin.json and README)
features.maintenance: pre-release, in active development — not public, no stars/releases; single squash commit (275149f "feat: initial Klarion", 2026-07-07), no tags, CHANGELOG has only an [Unreleased] 0.1.0 section; goreleaser/Homebrew tap are placeholders pending first tagged release
features.rule_count: 83 built-in rules — counted via `grep -c 'ID:' internal/rules/builtin.go` (83 unique rule IDs, from airtable-token to vercel-token, spanning cloud/vcs/ci/ai/payments/comms/db/infra/key categories); DESIGN.md section 12 describes the catalog as "50+ rules", so code exceeds the doc. Custom regex rules addable via [[rules.custom]] in .klarion.toml; `klarion rules list` shows the active set.
extras: MCP server: `klarion mcp` speaks JSON-RPC over stdio, exposing scan_text, scan_file, verify_finding (internal/mcp/tools.go); all responses redacted
Claude Code plugin (claude-plugin/): plugin.json v0.1.0 wiring hooks.json (PreToolUse on Write|Edit|MultiEdit + Bash matchers, 60s timeout) and mcp/servers.json, plus a /scan command
CI packaging: GitHub Action (action.yml), GitLab CI template (.gitlab/), Dockerfile + Dockerfile.goreleaser, .goreleaser.yaml, Makefile

Entropy engine (internal/entropy): Renyi(s, alpha), Shannon, Classify (smallest charset: digits < hex < lower/upper < alphanum < base64 < printable), ExpectedCollision, NormalizedScore; pure, dependency-free
Config: .klarion.toml discovered walking up from cwd, $KLARION_CONFIG / --config overrides, unknown keys are hard errors; tuned defaults layered
Scan controls: --fail-on severity, --no-ai, worker pool (default NumCPU), 1 MiB file-size skip, binary sniff via NUL in first 8 KiB, per-line/per-file finding caps
Privacy: send_secret toggle for redacted-only AI requests; secrets never serialized to reports/logs/MCP/hook output
Testing: 92 test functions across internal packages, hermetic (no network)

Benchmark harness (benchmark/): leaky/flask/rails datasets, accuracy.json + timing results; on the leaky dataset (heuristic-only): 45.45% file coverage, 22.29% find coverage, 0 out-of-ground-truth files flagged
Doc/code discrepancy: README's `klarion git --all` is implemented as `klarion git --history`

features.version: Installed: 3.93.5 (local `trufflehog --version`; released 2026-02-26 per GitHub API). Latest upstream: v3.95.8 (2026-07-02).
features.approach: Keyword-anchored regex detectors (~1,000 credential-type-specific detectors) run over chunked input from many sources, with chained decoders (base64/UTF-16/escaped-unicode/HTML) and live API verification of each candidate secret to classify results as verified/unverified/unknown.
features.verification: Yes — core differentiator. Each detector has programmatic verification against the service's API (e.g. AWS detector calls GetCallerIdentity); README: "over 700 credential detectors that support active verification against their respective APIs". Result statuses: verified / unverified / unknown (verification errored) / filtered_unverified, selectable via --results. Disable with --no-verification; custom verification endpoints via --verifier and --custom-verifiers-only; verification response caching (--no-verification-cache); private keys verified via Driftwood (checked against GitHub users / TLS certs). Sources: README FAQ + local --help.
features.git_history: Yes — `trufflehog git <uri>` scans full commit history (https://, ssh://, file:// repos). Flags (local --help): --since-commit, --branch, --max-depth (commit depth), --bare (for pre-receive hooks), --exclude-globs (filters at `git log` level), --clone-path/--no-cleanup, --trust-local-git-config. Also github/gitlab org-wide scanning and github-experimental object-discovery for hidden/deleted commit data.
features.precommit: Yes — official .pre-commit-hooks.yaml in repo root (id: trufflehog; entry: `trufflehog git file://. --since-commit HEAD --results=verified --fail --trust-local-git-config`). README also documents git hook usage and states "Available as a GitHub Action and a pre-commit hook". Source: raw.githubusercontent.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/main/.pre-commit-hooks.yaml.
features.baseline: No baseline/audit file workflow (unlike detect-secrets). FP suppression is primarily live verification: run with --results=verified to emit only API-confirmed secrets. Other mechanisms (local --help + README): inline `trufflehog:ignore` comment on the secret's line (for sources with line numbers); -i/--include-paths and -x/--exclude-paths (files of newline-separated regexes); --exclude-globs; --include-detectors/--exclude-detectors (by protobuf name/ID/range); --filter-entropy=N (drop low-Shannon-entropy unverified results, suggested 3.0); --filter-unverified (first unverified result per chunk per detector); --detector-timeout; --fail exits 183 when results found (CI gating).
features.output_formats: Colorized human-readable text (default), JSON (-j/--json), legacy pre-v3 JSON (--json-legacy; git/gitlab/github sources only), GitHub Actions annotation format (--github-actions). Source: local --help.

features.language: Python (GitHub API reports language=Python, ~99% per repo page); requires Python 3.10-3.12 per v1.5.0 release notes
features.approach: Plugin-based scanning combining three strategies: regex detectors for structured secrets (AWS, GitHub, Stripe, etc.), Shannon-entropy detection for random-looking strings (Base64HighEntropyString default limit 4.5, HexHighEntropyString default limit 3.0, tunable via --base64-limit/--hex-limit), and a KeywordDetector for suspicious variable names — followed by a filter layer that discards likely false positives (source: README + local `detect-secrets scan --help`).
features.verification: Yes, optionally. Some detectors verify candidate secrets via live network calls; verification is on by default and controlled by `-n/--no-verify` (disable) and `--only-verified` (only flag secrets that verify) — both shown in local `detect-secrets scan --help`. In the installed 1.5.0 package, 9 plugins implement verify(): aws, slack, stripe, mailchimp, softlayer, cloudant, ibm_cloud_iam, ibm_cos_hmac, telegram_token (verified by grepping detect_secrets/plugins/ in the installed site-packages).
features.git_history: Does NOT scan full git history. It scans the current state of git-tracked files (or all files with `--all-files`), and the pre-commit hook checks diffs of newly committed content. README explicitly states it "avoids the overhead of digging through all git history, as well as the need to scan the entire repository every time" (source: README; `--all-files` flag from local scan --help).
features.precommit: Yes — ships a `detect-secrets-hook` entry point with a first-class pre-commit framework integration: repo https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets, rev v1.5.0, hook id `detect-secrets`, args ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline'] (source: README pre-commit snippet; scan --help states output "is compatible with `detect-secrets-hook --baseline`").
features.baseline: Core design: a `.secrets.baseline` JSON file snapshots known/existing secrets so only NEW secrets fail checks; `detect-secrets audit` interactively labels findings as true/false positives (plus --diff to compare baselines, --stats analytics, --report). Inline allowlisting via `# pragma: allowlist secret` comments (with `--only-allowlisted` to re-verify them). Additional suppression: --exclude-lines/--exclude-files/--exclude-secrets regexes, built-in heuristic filters (is_sequential_string, is_likely_id_string, is_potential_uuid, is_lock_file, is_swagger_file, is_templated_secret, etc. — verified in installed filters/heuristic.py), optional wordlist and ML gibberish filters, and custom filters via `-f` (sources: local scan/audit --help, README, installed package).
features.output_formats: JSON only: `scan` writes a JSON baseline to stdout (optionally `--slim`); `audit --stats --json` gives machine-readable analytics; `audit --report` prints a findings report (with --only-real/--only-false). No built-in SARIF/CSV/HTML (sources: local --help outputs, README).

features.version: 0.1.11 (local: `ripsecrets --version` reports "ripsecrets 0.1.11", installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/ripsecrets; latest GitHub release tag v0.1.11, 2025-05-27)
features.language: Rust (GitHub API language field; built on ripgrep's grep/ignore/regex crates per src/lib.rs)
features.approach: Compiles ~28 known-provider regex patterns plus one keyword-anchored generic detector (lines containing key/token/secret/password) into a single combined regex, then filters generic matches through a statistical randomness test (p_random) instead of Shannon entropy, scanning files in parallel via ripgrep's directory walker (src/lib.rs and src/matcher/mod.rs at tag v0.1.11).
features.verification: No live verification. README design principle "Always local operation": it "will never send data off of your computer"; no network validation of candidate secrets (source: README at github.com/sirwart/ripsecrets).
features.git_history: Does not scan git history. It scans files/directories on disk (default '.'); pre-commit usage scans only staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM` piped as arguments (README pre-commit section; local --help says "searches files and directories recursively"). No commit/history traversal feature exists.
features.precommit: First-class: `--install-pre-commit` flag installs it as a git pre-commit hook automatically (local --help), `--strict-ignore` exists specifically for pre-commit invocation (local --help), and it ships pre-commit-framework hooks `ripsecrets` (builds via Rust) and `ripsecrets-system` (uses PATH binary) for .pre-commit-config.yaml (README).
features.baseline: .secretsignore file with gitignore-style path exclusion patterns plus an optional [secrets] section that allowlists specific secret values (loaded into an ignore_secrets HashSet in src/matcher/mod.rs); detect-secrets-compatible inline comment `# pragma: allowlist secret` on the matching line; `--strict-ignore` makes explicitly-passed paths also honor .secretsignore. No audited-baseline-file workflow like detect-secrets' baseline JSON (README + src/matcher/mod.rs).
features.output_formats: Plain grep-style text only: prints file, line number, and the matching line (termcolor-colored), with `--only-matching` to print just the matched secret; exits non-zero when secrets are found. No JSON/SARIF/CSV output flags (local --help; README).

extras: Randomness test instead of entropy: p_random() (src/matcher/p_random.rs) computes the probability a candidate string occurred by random chance; is_random() rejects candidates with p < 1e-5, and requires p >= 1e-4 if the string contains no digits (src/matcher/mod.rs at v0.1.11) — README describes flagging strings with >= ~1-in-10,000 chance of being random

Generic detection is keyword-anchored: random strings are only flagged when on a line matching key/token/secret/password followed by an assignment operator, 15-90 chars long (RANDOM_STRING_REGEX in src/matcher/mod.rs)

Speed as a headline feature: all patterns joined into one combined regex, parallel walker capped at min(12, num_cpus) threads via ripgrep's ignore crate; README benchmark on the Sentry repo (M1 MacBook Air): ripsecrets 0.32s vs trufflehog 31.2s (~95x) and detect-secrets 73.5s (~226x)
--additional-pattern custom regexes: if the regex contains a capture group, the captured group is itself tested for randomness before being reported (local --help)
Strictly local/offline by design — no telemetry, no network calls (README design principles)
Single static binary, no runtime dependencies; installable via Homebrew, prebuilt release binaries, cargo install from git, or Nix flake (README)
Respects .gitignore during recursive scans (uses ripgrep's ignore crate) and supports .secretsignore as a custom ignore filename (src/lib.rs)
No JSON/SARIF/baseline-audit/git-history features — deliberately narrow pre-commit-focused scope compared to trufflehog/gitleaks/detect-secrets
